CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Game.Note: The world re-entry recovery added two lines only: the IReentryControl constructor parameter and the one-line pump call of a step that lives in its own domain (ReentryCoordinator), which is the watchlist's rule for this file. The remote-backpack access rule added the RemoteVitalsService/ILocalizationService/AnnouncedHostRules constructor parameters plus the one-line notice wiring they feed (+5 lines): all three feed the coordinator and the drag dispatcher, and the announced rules are what a MEMBER's local check reads (decision 263), so the adapter passes them through rather than owning them. The give's answer-first wiring added the IRemotePlacementResolver constructor parameter and the one per-frame placement pump (+2 lines), both pass-throughs to a domain that owns the behaviour. The spectator-mode ruling added three one-line forwardings of the mode (IsSpectator, EnterSpectatorMode, ExitSpectatorMode) to SpectatorCameraService, which owns the state (+3 lines, plus the separating blank lines), and the cycling strip added the fourth forwarding (IsFreeFly, +2 lines with its blank line), then the mirror switch the fifth (MirrorEffects as a forwarding property, +4 lines with its accessors and blank line), the native loading-text surface the sixth (WaitingTextIsOnTheNativeScreen, a one-line forwarding of StartGateCoordinator's own property, +2 lines with its blank line), and the intro cover's decision the seventh (the static IntroCoverDecision, its three-line log hook and the second IJoinFlowPresentation member, +7 lines): every one of these is a forwarding to a domain or a named decision that owns the rule, which is why the file grows rather than absorbs. The end-of-layer panel's ownership added the eighth (one per-frame call into LayerAdvanceCoordinator.UpdatePanelChoices, +2 lines): the panel's two choices belong to the host, and the hiding lives in the coordinator that already owns the panel's wiring; the panel's VISIBILITY added the ninth (one per-frame call into LayerPanelGate.Update, +1 line), which decides from the living group's share and owns that rule in its own class. The seam a split owes is still the patch-bridge forwarding half; the end-of-layer panel's LATE-FRAME write added the tenth (the ILayerPanelVisibilityPump implementation, +6 lines with its doc comment), because the panel must be written after the game's own WorldGeneration.Update and that phase belongs to the host shell. The custody projection added the eleventh (one per-frame call into ItemCustodyProjection.Tick, +5 lines with its comment): it is a SHADOW comparison that changes nothing, and the tick belongs here because the frame pump is the adapter's; stage 2 of docs/backlog/review/item-custody-single-authority.md moves the comparison to whatever replaces the five stores, and this line goes with them.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Run..Note: The host-descent follow added the descent state machine, its scene-state guards, the settle edge, the abort paths (world lost, hold/settle timeouts) and the release branches; the independent review's blocker and majors then added the abort policy, the menu-return origin guard and the baseline-cancel branch — the guest's new-layer generation itself remains the game's own coroutine, started from LayerAdvanceCoordinator. This is the top of this file's split list.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Char.Note: The host-state cycle added the local injury trigger and the owner-state report; the heal authority fix added the applied-reset retry tick and its body/session drop (the retry state itself lives in Runtime's HealResetReportRetry); the craft-report fix added the owner-addressed RetireCarriedItem delegation the session binding calls (+2 code lines and its doc), which is the domain's own seam, not new state; the host-descent follow added the saved-character handback refusal for the body that came through it (a Func seam the composition binds to the run's preserved-body fact), and the descent-spawn follow added the snapshot's layer stamp (reports and the local cut) and the restore's stale-layer position refusal. The planned split is still the trigger into LocalInjuryReporter (owning the baseline, the host-row absorption and the report call), leaving the coordinator the snapshot/restore/render seams.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.Runtime.Session..Note: The heal authority event added the applied-reset send seam (whose verdict the caller must see) after the event-merge seams moved into CharacterEventMerges; the descent-spawn follow only expanded the handback's comment (the save's kernel projection makes the respawn alive before this send, so the send's projection confirms it). The planned split is still the host-model companion (advance marks + refusal window) fed by this store, leaving the table the save/restore and the report filter.

The world re-entry recovery added the HasCommittedRunBaseline read (the fact the targeted world-join's baseline promise is made from) to the world facade, which stood at 598 across its two partial files. The host-descent edge added its three pass-throughs (send, fire, event) whose flow lives in LayerDescentChannel; the descent-spawn follow added the CurrentGeneration read (the kernel run baseline stamp a character snapshot is captured in). The next split here takes those pass-throughs with the report-recovery ones the second partial's own comment names.

The world surface's contract. The descent-spawn follow added the CurrentGeneration read — the kernel run baseline stamp a character snapshot is captured in, which the CharacterData restore compares against its own layer. The spectator notice added its four members (send, relay, fire and the event), all forwarding to SpectatorNoticeChannel. The interface has no state; its size is the world/persistence surface collected here, and the next grower owes the per-domain port extraction the facade's own split plan names.

The give's answer-first custody added the exact-destination rung (ExactDestinationSlot and the two sentences that name a destination the receiver's answer lost), which took the class past 600; the return half was moved out again into GivenItemReturnService, so this is the forward custody alone. The split this owes is the destination resolution (this class's slot/container/slot-substitution rules and the ladder's candidate ordering) into their own object, the shape LocalBodyPlacement already gives the adapter side; the custody core, the kernel bookkeeping and the transfer publication stay here. Recorded rather than split in this change because the acceptance rows must run against the same class the earlier batches read.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Play.Note: The receiving half of a cross-player transfer: it applies the custody answer on the side it names. It reached 601 with the ruling that a give no longer plays a sound of its own (the release click is the game own, and the cloth belongs to container moves), which removed a call and left the comments that explain why beside it. The split this owes is one applier per direction (give, take, return) behind the dispatch it already has.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Remo.Note: The receiver half of the remote intents: one method per intent kind, each replaying the game own call on the owner real objects. It crossed 600 with the ground hand-over (a world item resolved through the scene and placed by the receiver own native pickup) and with the detach-before-place step that keeps a cross-player give from playing the container sound the native slot move never plays. The split this owes is one applier per intent family (drop/container, slot, use/wear, battery/trader) behind the same dispatch, the shape RemoteIntentSlotRelease already gives one shared sub-rule.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.IPat.Note: The aggregate is the patch layer's one seam list: every hook the patches read is a member here, so it grows with each landed hook instead of absorbing behaviour — the members forward to the domains that own the rules. It crossed 600 with the radiation line's two facts, RadiationLineCeiling (the host rule's floor stop) and RadiationLineGuestTimeGone (the member's line value extrapolated at the HOST's rate, the user's 2026-10-24 finding that a member's descent ran at its own body's speed). Both are pure projections of domain state, which is why they belong on the seam rather than in a patch. The seam a split owes is the same one the other patch-layer rows name: the interface is a list of hooks, and its size is the number of things the game lets us observe.

CasualtiesUnknownOnline.GameAdapter.Game.Note: The host-descent edge added the ILayerAdvancePatchPort member and the generation-launch notification on ResetGenStreamToBaseline — both forward to their domains.
